title: The History of The Elder Scrolls | From Arena To Oblivion Remastered | Gaming History
description: The full history of Bethesda's Elder Scrolls series: Arena in 1994, Daggerfall, Morrowind, Oblivion, Skyrim, the online game, the 2025 Oblivion remaster and the wait for number six.

sections.heading: A world with no walls
sections.script: You wake up on a cart, a stranger shouts at you, and a dragon lands on a tower. Then the game lets you walk wherever you like. That freedom is the heart of The Elder Scrolls, one of the most loved role playing series ever made. It has given us Morrowind's alien islands, Oblivion's gates to hell, and Skyrim, a game that people still play and mod more than a decade later. In this video we trace the whole history, from a small sports game studio that took a gamble in nineteen ninety four, to the shock release of the Oblivion remaster in twenty twenty five. Along the way we will look at the mods, the dragons, the online game and the long wait for the next chapter. Grab a torch, because we are heading into Tamriel.

sections.heading: From sports games to Arena
sections.script: Before The Elder Scrolls, the studio Bethesda was mostly known for sports games and for games based on movies, including the Terminator. In the early nineteen nineties a small team there decided to try a fantasy role playing game. It began life as a gladiator fighting game, which is where the name Arena came from. As development went on, the tournaments faded away and the quests and dungeons took over, but the printed packaging already said Arena, so the name stayed. The game was missing its Christmas nineteen ninety three target and came out in early nineteen ninety four. At first the distributors were nervous and only a small number of copies shipped. Yet word of mouth kept it selling month after month, and it became a cult hit that proved there was an audience for huge open fantasy worlds on the computer.

sections.heading: Daggerfall goes enormous
sections.script: The sequel, Daggerfall, arrived in September nineteen ninety six and pushed the idea much further. The team built a game world often described as roughly the size of Great Britain, and used one of the first truly three dimensional engines the studio had made. You could design your own class, pick your own skills, and join guilds, temples and noble houses. Daggerfall also introduced the style of lore that fans still love: gods, rival cults and political schemes explained through books and rumours instead of one narrator. Like Arena, it launched with bugs, and players were not shy about saying so. The experience taught Bethesda to be more careful with release schedules. Two smaller side games followed, Battlespire and Redguard, which did not do well with fans who wanted vast worlds, so the studio went back to thinking big.

sections.heading: Morrowind, the strange one
sections.script: In May of two thousand two came Morrowind, and many fans still call it the most original game in the series. Instead of a standard fantasy kingdom, you arrived on Vvardenfell, an island of giant mushrooms, towering insect shells and huge ash storms. The team tripled its staff and built the world by hand, rather than letting the computer generate it. They also created the Construction Set, a tool that let outsiders build their own quests and places. That one tool launched an entire modding culture that still defines the series. The game released first on computer and then on the Xbox, and won Game of the Year awards from several outlets. Two expansions, Tribunal and Bloodmoon, added a walled city and a frozen northern island.

sections.heading: Oblivion opens the gates
sections.script: Oblivion launched on March twenty first, two thousand six, for the Xbox three sixty and computers. It followed a fresh story about the Oblivion Crisis, where gates to a hellish plane open and demons pour into the land. Bethesda focused on a tighter story, better characters and a more cinematic look, with improved artificial intelligence and physics. The developers also used procedural tools to build the landscape faster, which let the team make lush forests and hills across a large province. Oblivion became famous for its funny voice acting, its thieves guild and its Dark Brotherhood questline. Two downloadable expansions arrived, Knights of the Nine and Shivering Isles, and Oblivion joined Morrowind as a Game of the Year winner, which made the series a true mainstream name.

sections.heading: Skyrim and the dragons
sections.script: Then came Skyrim, released on November eleventh, two thousand eleven. Set in a cold land inspired by Scandinavia, it tells the story of the Dragonborn, a hero who can absorb the power of dragons and must stop Alduin the World Eater. Skyrim changed how skills and levels worked, so that the more you used a skill, the more it helped you grow. It won Game of the Year from many outlets, and three add ons followed in twenty twelve: Dawnguard with vampires, Hearthfire with house building, and Dragonborn on the island of Solstheim. The Special Edition came in October twenty sixteen. Skyrim is also the series' sales monster. In twenty twenty three, Bethesda's Todd Howard said it had sold more than sixty million copies.

sections.heading: Why Skyrim never dies
sections.script: A big reason Skyrim has lasted so long is its community. Thanks to the Creation Kit and its tools, players have made thousands of mods that change everything from graphics to entire new quest lines. The game also came back again and again on new systems, including a virtual reality version in twenty seventeen, and even became a joke about being on every device. Another reason is how the game feels. You can ignore the main story and become a thief, a mage or a farmer who lives in a house you built. Quests grow out of exploration, so a random cave can turn into a story. Because of that, many players say they never truly finish Skyrim, they just stop playing for a while and then return.

sections.heading: The Elder Scrolls Online
sections.script: While fans waited for another single player chapter, Bethesda's sister studio, ZeniMax Online Studios, built a different kind of game. The Elder Scrolls Online was revealed in May twenty twelve and launched on computers in April twenty fourteen, with console versions arriving in June twenty fifteen. It lets you visit almost all of Tamriel together with other players, in a time long before the single player games. At first it asked for a monthly subscription, but that requirement was dropped in March twenty fifteen, and an optional membership called ESO Plus took its place. The game has kept growing through yearly story seasons and new regions. There were also spin offs, including the card game Legends and the mobile game Blades, but the online game is the one that has stayed alive for the long run.

sections.heading: Oblivion returns
sections.script: On April twenty second, twenty twenty five, Bethesda surprised everyone with a shadow drop. During a live stream it revealed The Elder Scrolls four, Oblivion Remastered, and released it that same day. The remaster was made together with the studio Virtuos, and rebuilt the visuals with modern technology while keeping the original game underneath. It reached over one hundred eighty thousand players at the same time on Steam, and Bethesda said it passed four million players within the first days. Reviews were warm, though some players grumbled about the price and a few technical problems. The surprise launch also showed that people are hungry for new Elder Scrolls content, and that a classic can find a new audience twenty years after it first came out.

sections.heading: The long wait for number six
sections.script: The Elder Scrolls six was first shown in a short teaser at the E3 show in twenty eighteen, alongside Starfield. Since then Bethesda has not announced a release date, and Todd Howard has asked fans to be patient. Microsoft bought Bethesda's parent company in twenty twenty one, and the game is expected on Xbox and computers. We should be careful here, because there are no confirmed details about its setting. Fans guess Hammerfell or High Rock, but those are only guesses. What we do know is the pattern. Each Elder Scrolls game has taken the series somewhere new, from the arena cities to Morrowind's ash lands and Skyrim's snowy peaks. Whatever comes next will have a huge mountain to climb, but if history is any guide, it will be worth the wait.

sections.heading: Which Elder Scrolls is yours
sections.script: Let us wrap up the journey. A small studio took a risk in nineteen ninety four with Arena, made a giant world in Daggerfall, wowed us with the weird beauty of Morrowind, brought hell to the screen in Oblivion, and then gave us dragons in Skyrim. Along the way came an online world, a surprise remaster, and mods that keep the games alive. The series teaches that players love freedom and a world that rewards curiosity more than anything else. So here is the big question. Which Elder Scrolls game is your favourite, and which race and class did you pick for your first character? Tell us in the comments, and if you enjoyed this history, subscribe for more franchise stories. Thanks for watching, and may you walk on warm sands.
